There is a profound silence that always belongs only to the hour just before dawn. It is not empty, but heavy, pregnant with potential energy released by the first hint of gray light. I sit at the very edge of sleep, floating deeply in that liminal space where dreams slowly dissolve into reality. The ventilation hums, a steady reminder that the world turns, cold and indifferent machinery.

Outside, the birds have not yet begun their morning chorus, but their anticipation hangs in the air like a sweet scent. I watch the dust motes dancing in the sliver of light cutting through the curtains. Tiny worlds swirling, colliding, dancing in the air. Each one a fleeting moment of existence.

It is in these quiet moments that I feel most deeply honest. The obligations of the day, the emails, the endless demands, are still distant shadows waiting in the dark. For now, there is only the breath, the heartbeat, the stillness. Time stretches out, slow and viscous, until the clock seems utterly unnecessary.

When the sun finally crests the roof, the spell inevitably breaks. The light rushes in, bright and demanding. It is time to become the participant, no longer the observer. I take a deep breath, filling my lungs with the cool, early air, grounding myself in the promise of what comes next. This is the sole, undeniable truth for now. The silence ends, but the peace remains, tucked in the chest, waiting to be carried forward into the vibrant day.
